issues.issue: Is the claimant's account credible, despite his UK claim and the different story given there?
issues.applicant_position: Claimant says his different UK account was fabricated on his agent's advice, and his core account of LTTE pressure and arrest is true.
issues.respondent_position: Minister argues the claimant lacks objective and subjective fear and generally lacked credibility.
issues.result_quote: I have found the claimant to be a credible witness and therefore believe what he has alleged in support of his claim.

issues.issue: Does the claimant face a well-founded fear of persecution or personal risk from Sri Lankan authorities on return as a Tamil with an arrest record?
issues.applicant_position: Claimant says he was arrested in Colombo after an attack on an army officer, so authorities will arrest and mistreat him on return.
issues.respondent_position: Minister argues the two-day release shows authorities did not regard him as an LTTE activist, so he is unlikely to be targeted.
issues.result_quote: However, I find that the claimant now has a well founded fear of persecution and a personal risk of harm by the Sri Lankan authorities.

issues.issue: Is state protection available to the claimant from Sri Lankan authorities?
issues.applicant_position: Claimant says the state is the agent of persecution, so state protection would not be reasonably forthcoming.
issues.respondent_position: Minister relies on an email and article suggesting the Sri Lankan Army guarantees security for a referred combatant.
issues.result_quote: The panel has also considered whether state protection is available to the claimant and concluded that it is not.

issues.issue: Is there a viable internal flight alternative anywhere in Sri Lanka for the claimant?
issues.result_quote: I therefore find that he has no viable internal flight alternative available to him.
